arxiv-1907-12792.title: A General Relativistic Approach to Small-Scale Structure Formation
arxiv-1907-12792.creator: Dipanjan Dey, Prashant Kocherlakota, Pankaj S. Joshi
arxiv-1907-12792.description: Abstract We treat here general relativistically the issue of galaxy formation, which is a major problem in cosmology. While the current models use a top-hat collapse model, coupled with Newtonian virialization technique to balance the gravitationally collapsing matter cloud into a galaxy, we present here a general relativistic toy model to achieve such a purpose.

arxiv-2006-06114.title: Consolidating Commonsense Knowledge
arxiv-2006-06114.creator:
ame Filip Ilievski \email ilievski@isi.edu, 
ame Jingwei Cheng \email chengjingwei@mail.neu.edu.cn, 
ame Ehsan Qasemi \email qasemi@isi.edu
arxiv-2006-06114.description: Abstract Commonsense reasoning is an important aspect of building robust AI systems and is receiving significant attention in the natural language understanding, computer vision, and knowledge graphs communities. At present, a number of valuable commonsense knowledge sources exist, with different foci, strengths, and weaknesses. In this paper, we list representative sources and their properties.

arxiv-2107-03104.title: MACCIF-TDNN: MULTI ASPECT AGGREGATION OF CHANNEL AND CONTEXT INTERDEPENDENCE FEATURES IN TDNN-based SPEAKER VERIFICATION
arxiv-2107-03104.creator: F ​ a ​ n ​ g ​ y ​ u ​ a ​ n Fangyuan W ​ a ​ n ​ g Wan{g}, Z ​ h ​ i ​ g ​ a ​ n ​ g Zhigang S ​ o ​ n ​ g Son{g}, H ​ o ​ n ​ g ​ c ​ h ​ e ​ n Hongchen J ​ i ​ a ​ n ​ g Jian{g}, B ​ o Bo X ​ u X{u}
arxiv-2107-03104.description: Abstract Most of the recent state-of-the-art results for speaker verification are achieved by X-vector and its subsequent variants. In this paper, we propose a new network architecture which aggregates the channel and context interdependence features from multi aspect based on Time Delay Neural Network (TDNN).

arxiv-2212-04092.title: Successive Prompting for Decomposing Complex Questions
arxiv-2212-04092.creator: Dheeru Dua Shivanshu Gupta Sameer Singh Matt Gardner
arxiv-2212-04092.description: Abstract Answering complex questions that require making latent decisions is a challenging task, especially when limited supervision is available. Recent works leverage the capabilities of large language models (LMs) to perform complex question answering in a few-shot setting by demonstrating how to output intermediate rationalizations while solving the complex question in a single pass.

arxiv-2401-06553.title: Probing charge of compact objects with gravitational microlensing of gravitational waves
arxiv-2401-06553.creator: Uddeepta Deka, Sumanta Chakraborty, Shasvath J. Kapadia, Md Arif Shaikh, Parameswaran Ajith
arxiv-2401-06553.description: Abstract Gravitational microlensing of gravitational waves (GWs) opens up the exciting possibility of studying the spacetime geometry around the lens. In this work, we investigate the prospects of constraining the ‘charged’ hair of a charged gravitating object from the observation of a GW signal microlensed by the same. The charge can have electromagnetic or modified gravity origin.

arxiv-2410-22427.title: RR Lyrae stars trace the Milky Way warp
arxiv-2410-22427.creator: Mauro Cabrera-Gadea, Cecilia Mateu, Pau Ramos
arxiv-2410-22427.description: Abstract Context. The outskirts of the Milky Way disc have been known to be warped since the late 1950s. Although various stellar populations have shown an underlying warped distribution, the relation between the age of the population and the warp they trace remains an open question.

arxiv-2412-19816.title: From terrestrial weather to space weather through the history of scintillation
arxiv-2412-19816.creator: Emily F. Kerrison 1,2,3, Ron D. Ekers 3, John Morgan 4 & Rajan Chhetri 4
arxiv-2412-19816.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Emily F. Kerrison 1,2,3, Ron D. Ekers 3, John Morgan 4 & Rajan Chhetri 4. Recent observations of interplanetary scintillation (IPS) at radio frequencies have proved to be a powerful tool for probing the solar environment from the ground. But how far back does this tradition really extend?

arxiv-2601-13504.title: Modeling Age-Adjusted Mortality in the United States
arxiv-2601-13504.creator: Brandon Dunbar, Paramahansa Pramanik, Haley Kate Robinson
arxiv-2601-13504.description: Abstract This research explores how total mortality figures relate to age-standardized death rates within the United States, using the complete historical record of national mortality statistics. Through a detailed investigation of both all-cause and cause-specific mortality trends, the study evaluates the impact of demographic standardization on interpreting mortality data across different time periods and geographic regions.

arxiv-2602-18160.title: Unifying Formal Explanations: A Complexity-Theoretic Perspective
arxiv-2602-18160.creator: Shahaf Bassan, Xuanxiang Huang, Guy Katz, The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Nanyang Technological University shahaf.bassan@mail.huji.ac.il, xuanxiang.huang@ntu.edu.sg,g.katz@mail.huji.ac.il
arxiv-2602-18160.description: Abstract Previous work has explored the computational complexity of deriving two fundamental types of explanations for ML model predictions: (i) sufficient reasons , which are subsets of input features that, when fixed, determine a prediction, and (ii) contrastive reasons , which are subsets of input features that, when modified, alter a prediction .

pmc-10742799.creator: Vera Stara, Margherita Rampioni, Adrian Alexandru Moșoi, Dominic M. Kristaly, Sorin-Aurel Moraru, Lucia Paciaroni, Susy Paolini, Alessandra Raccichini, Elisa Felici, Giacomo Cucchieri, Luca Antognoli, Alessandra Millevolte, Marina Antici, Mirko di Rosa

pmc-11483792.title: An Active Trend of Immunotherapy Combination Regimen as Second-Line Therapy Towards Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer
pmc-11483792.creator: Haimin Weng, Pengfei Zeng, Yuemiao Chen, Qi Xu, Jieer Ying
pmc-11483792.description: Background:As a second-line therapy, oxaliplatin/fluorouracil/leucovorin (FOLFOX) remains the standard of care for patients with biliary tract cancer (BTC); however, its efficacy is suboptimal. The aim of this study was to evaluate whether, compared with chemotherapy alone, the immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) combination regimen improved the overall survival (OS) in patients with advanced BTC.

pmc-12372174.title: The grit personality trait, eating behavior, and obesity among Japanese adults: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12372174.creator: Noriaki Kurita, Takako Maeshibu, Tetsuro Aita, Takafumi Wakita, Hiroe Kikuchi
pmc-12372174.description: BackgroundObesity is a chronic disease influenced by genetic, cultural, environmental, and psychosocial factors, making it difficult to manage through individual effort alone. Despite this complexity, obesity is often attributed to a lack of willpower and poor control over eating behaviors, contributing to stigma. However, research on this issue remains limited.

pmc-12639583.creator: Gunnar Johansson, Jonas Reinold, Nelly L Shapero, Tekla L Rosell, Leif A Jørgensen, Niklas Koenen, Christian Frøsig, Michael Falkenberg, Lene Holdrup, Kristian Juul

ObjectiveThis real-life analysis quantifies the incidence rate of diagnosed hyponatraemia in patients treated with a desmopressin Orally Disintegrating Tablet 25–50 μg (ODT) versus patients treated for lower urinary tract symptoms (LUTS) across Sweden, Denmark, and Germany.Material and methodsClaims data and register data from drug registries, hospital records, laboratories, and intensive care units were accessed from the three countries in this imposed Post-Authorisation Safety Study (PASS).

pmc-12644684.title: Optical trapping with optical magnetic field and photonic Hall effect forces
pmc-12644684.creator: Yanzeng Li, Emmanuel Valenton, Spoorthi Nagasamudram, John Parker, Marcos Perez, Uttam Manna, Mahua Biswas, Stuart A Rice, Norbert F Scherer
pmc-12644684.description: Optical trapping offers robust nanoscale control of matter but, to date, has been dominated by the interaction between a material’s electric polarizability, αe, and the electric part of light, therefore defined by electric-field intensity-gradient forces. Magnetic light-matter interactions, despite their potential to reshape optical trapping research, have remained experimentally unrealized.

pmc-13197929.title: Adiposity Rebound or Fat-Free Mass Anabolism in Children—Challenging a 42-Year-Old BMI Puzzle with Waist-to-Height Ratio: The ASNF-NNF 2025 Inaugural Flemming Quaade Award for Innovation in Childhood Obesity Lecture
pmc-13197929.creator: Andrew O Agbaje
pmc-13197929.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundRolland-Cachera et al. introduced the concept of “adiposity rebound” in a paper published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 1984. They observed that body mass index (BMI) increased during the first year of life and then decreased with a renewed rise at about age 6 y, which they termed “adiposity rebound,” concluding that early rebound increased the risk of excess adiposity in later years.

pmc-13429505.creator: Kai Chen, Huifang Wang, Qing Liu, Guanhua Hu, Zhang Feng, Bing Zou, Yingxi Zuo, Lu Bai, Pan Suo, Jingbo Shao, Hui Jiang, Xiaohui Zhang, Xiaojun Huang, Jinjin Chen, Yifei Cheng
pmc-13429505.description: BackgroundThe clinical efficacy and prognostic factors of haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (haplo-HSCT) as a salvage approach for children with relapsed acute leukemia (AL) after a first allogeneic HSCT (allo-HSCT) remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy, survival outcomes, and prognostic factors of second haploidentical HSCT in children with relapsed AL following prior allo-HSCT.

pmc-13633791.title: Comparing the pain relief effectiveness of intravenous magnesium sulfate and ketorolac versus intravenous morphine and ketorolac for kidney stones
pmc-13633791.creator: Mehdi Fallah Bagher Sheydaei, Ahmad R. Baghernezhad, Ali Bakhtiari, Faezeh Rezaei
pmc-13633791.description: BACKGROUND:Pain is one of the most common symptoms in various diseases. While morphine is widely used for pain relief, its adverse effects and potential for misuse have led to the exploration of safer alternatives. This study aimed to compare the analgesic effectiveness of intravenous magnesium sulfate versus morphine, both in combination with ketorolac, in patients with renal colic.
